The [Air Pollutants Emissions Methodology for the Logistics Sector﻿](https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/Report_AP.pdf) signifies a significant advancement in environmental reporting by broadening the scope of reported emissions to include air pollutant emissions, in addition to greenhouse gases. This methodology, which has been based on the CCAC and SEI [Integrated guide for business greenhouse gas and air pollutant emission assessment﻿](https://www.sei.org/publications/integrated-guide-for-business-greenhouse-gas-and-air-pollutant-emission-assessment/), has been incorporated into the very well-established [Global Logistics Emissions Council (GLEC) Framework﻿](https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3.2_21_10_25_1.pdf), adopted by over 200 multinational corporations and aligned with [ISO 14083:2023﻿](https://www.iso.org/standard/78864.html). The GLEC Framework is designed for carriers, logistics service providers, shippers, and policymakers looking to enhance transparency and decision-making. It aligns with major international standards, such as the [Greenhouse Gas Protocol﻿](https://ghgprotocol.org/sites/default/files/ghgp/standards/ghg-protocol-revised.pdf) and the [Carbon Disclosure Project﻿](https://www.cdp.net/en/disclose) (CDP). It also supports the goals of the [Science-Based Targets initiative﻿](https://sciencebasedtargets.org/standards-and-guidance) (SBTi).

This update to the GLEC framework will provide users with appropriate methods to quantify air pollutant emissions from all modes of transport—road, non-road mobile machinery, rail, aviation, and shipping. The users will be able to quantify emissions of nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulphur oxides (SOx), particulate matter (PM 10 ,PM 2.5), and black carbon (BC) and develop air pollutant emissions inventories that can be used for their sustainability reports or other types of reporting (e.g., under the [Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive﻿](https://finance.ec.europa.eu/regulation-and-supervision/financial-services-legislation/implementing-and-delegated-acts/corporate-sustainability-reporting-directive_en)).

Air pollution is the largest environmental [health risk﻿](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/ambient-(outdoor)-air-quality-and-health) and a major driver of climate and ecosystem degradation. The transport and logistics sectors contribute to air pollutant emissions primarily through fuel combustion, but also through non-exhaust emissions from tyre and brake wear. Addressing air pollutant emissions, wherever these occur within a company’s value chain and transport-related operations, can have substantial benefits on human and ecosystem health.

By integrating air pollutant emissions into existing GHG reporting, organizations can develop comprehensive inventories that enable them to understand the magnitude of air pollutant emissions, identify the largest sources, and determine where action should be taken to improve air quality and reduce air pollution.

[Download the methodology from SFC](https://smartfreightcentre.org/documents/769/Report_AP.pdf)

							<p>The <em>Air Pollutants Emissions Methodology for the Logistics Sector</em> provides guidance on measuring emissions in transportation logistics. Developed collaboratively by the Smart Freight Centre, SEI at the University of York, and the Clean Air Fund, it has been incorporated into the most recent version (v3.2) of the <a href="https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3.2_21_10_25_1.pdf" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>GLEC Framework</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿</span></a>. <section class="c-wysiwyg-block o-section  js-toc-content" lang="en">
	<div class="c-wysiwyg-block__container o-container">
		<div class="c-wysiwyg-block__wrapper o-content-from-editor">
			<p>The <a href="https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/Report_AP.pdf" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>Air Pollutants Emissions Methodology for the Logistics Sector</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿<svg class="o-svg o-svg--external-link "><use class="o-svg__use" href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link" xlink:href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link"></use></svg></span></a> signifies a significant advancement in environmental reporting by broadening the scope of reported emissions to include air pollutant emissions, in addition to greenhouse gases. This methodology, which has been based on the CCAC and SEI<a href="https://www.sei.org/publications/integrated-guide-for-business-greenhouse-gas-and-air-pollutant-emission-assessment/" target="_self"><span> Integrated guide for business greenhouse gas and air pollutant emission assessment</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿</span></a>, has been incorporated into the very well-established <a href="https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3.2_21_10_25_1.pdf" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>Global Logistics Emissions Council (GLEC) Framework</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿<svg class="o-svg o-svg--external-link "><use class="o-svg__use" href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link" xlink:href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link"></use></svg></span></a>, adopted by over 200 multinational corporations and aligned with <a href="https://www.iso.org/standard/78864.html" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>ISO 14083:2023</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿<svg class="o-svg o-svg--external-link "><use class="o-svg__use" href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link" xlink:href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link"></use></svg></span></a>. The GLEC Framework is designed for carriers, logistics service providers, shippers, and policymakers looking to enhance transparency and decision-making. It aligns with major international standards, such as the <a href="https://ghgprotocol.org/sites/default/files/ghgp/standards/ghg-protocol-revised.pdf" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>Greenhouse Gas Protocol</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿<svg class="o-svg o-svg--external-link "><use class="o-svg__use" href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link" xlink:href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link"></use></svg></span></a> and the <a href="https://www.cdp.net/en/disclose" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>Carbon Disclosure Project</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿<svg class="o-svg o-svg--external-link "><use class="o-svg__use" href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link" xlink:href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link"></use></svg></span></a> (CDP). It also supports the goals of the <a href="https://sciencebasedtargets.org/standards-and-guidance" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>Science-Based Targets initiative</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿<svg class="o-svg o-svg--external-link "><use class="o-svg__use" href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link" xlink:href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link"></use></svg></span></a> (SBTi).</p>
<p>This update to the GLEC framework will provide users with appropriate methods to quantify air pollutant emissions from all modes of transport—road, non-road mobile machinery, rail, aviation, and shipping. The users will be able to quantify emissions of nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulphur oxides (SOx), particulate matter (PM <sub>10 </sub>,PM <sub>2.5</sub>), and black carbon (BC) and develop air pollutant emissions inventories that can be used for their sustainability reports or other types of reporting (e.g., under the <a href="https://finance.ec.europa.eu/regulation-and-supervision/financial-services-legislation/implementing-and-delegated-acts/corporate-sustainability-reporting-directive_en" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿<svg class="o-svg o-svg--external-link "><use class="o-svg__use" href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link" xlink:href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link"></use></svg></span></a>).</p>
<p>Air pollution is the largest environmental <a href="https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/ambient-(outdoor)-air-quality-and-health" target="_blank" class="is-external"><span>health risk</span><span class="u-no-wrap-icon">﻿<svg class="o-svg o-svg--external-link "><use class="o-svg__use" href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link" xlink:href="https://www.sei.org/wp-content/themes/sei/assets/img/symbol/svg/sprite.symbol.svg?v=1788871790#external-link"></use></svg></span></a> and a major driver of climate and ecosystem degradation. The transport and logistics sectors contribute to air pollutant emissions primarily through fuel combustion, but also through non-exhaust emissions from tyre and brake wear. Addressing air pollutant emissions, wherever these occur within a company’s value chain and transport-related operations, can have substantial benefits on human and ecosystem health.</p>
<p>By integrating air pollutant emissions into existing GHG reporting, organizations can develop comprehensive inventories that enable them to understand the magnitude of air pollutant emissions, identify the largest sources, and determine where action should be taken to improve air quality and reduce air pollution.</p>
